newsitem.title: UK: Zambian cobalt airlift to Europe continues.
newsitem.headline: Zambian cobalt airlift to Europe continues.

text.p: DAS Air Cargo has been moving around 70 tonnes of cobalt a week from Zambia since the start of May and expects to continue doing so into June, ANA International director, Phil Thomsett told Reuters.
ANA is the UK general sales agent for DAS Air.
"We've being moving 36 tonnes on a scheduled weekly McDonnell Douglas DC-10-30 freighter out of Lusaka with the remainder on a Boeing 707 freighter, also carrying 36 tonnes," Thomsett said.
"We expect to hear next week that the contract will renewed for June," he said.
At end-April, DAS Air it had been moving 100 tonnes of Zambian cobalt to Antwerp and Rotterdam on a DC-10 and two Boeing 707 flights since March.

Key reasons for choosing airfreight for moving cobalt were that deliveries were late and losses of metal had been encountered when it was moved by rail from Zambia to Dar-es-Salaam, DAS Air officials said.
The airline is UK-managed but operates four Boeing 707 freighters in addition to the DC-10. A second DC-10 has been acquired and after conversion to a freighter will enter service late this year.
